chunks: Saʿd ibn Ṭarīf narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
ʿAlī عليه السلام ordered cutting in the case of an iron helmet and a shield whose weight was thirty-eight ratls.

key_terms.بَيْضَةِ: an iron helmet or headpiece of armor
key_terms.جُنَّةٍ: a shield used for protection in battle
key_terms.حَدِيدٍ: iron, describing the material of the helmet
key_terms.قَطَعَ: ordered amputation as a legal punishment
key_terms.وَزْنُهَا: its weight, indicating measurable value or amount

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the hadd punishment for stealing armor or a shield?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling attributed to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding the hadd punishment for theft. It indicates that stolen property such as an iron helmet or a shield of substantial weight could meet the threshold for amputation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5101 - Sa'd ibn Tarif narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:
"Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) ordered the cutting off of a hand for stealing an iron helmet and for a shield that weighed thirty-eight ratl (a unit of weight)."
